nodes.summary: Entry `(v, j)` is `σ j` if `b j = v` and `0` otherwise.
nodes.title: Entries of the boundary-column matrix

nodes.summary: The real `V × F` matrix whose column `j` is `σ j` times the standard basis vector at the anchor `b j`.
nodes.title: Boundary columns

nodes.summary: For a loopless finite multigraph, a real vector `r` lies in the range of `orientedIncidence end₁ end₂` if and only if its sum over the vertices of every connected component of `underlyingGraph end₁ end₂` vanishes.
nodes.title: Range of the oriented incidence matrix

nodes.summary: If the endpoints of `e` are distinct, the entry of `orientedIncidence end₁ end₂` at `(end₂ e, e)` is `-1`.
nodes.title: Second-endpoint entry

nodes.summary: If the endpoints of `e` are distinct, the entry of `orientedIncidence end₁ end₂` at `(end₁ e, e)` is `1`.
nodes.title: First-endpoint entry

nodes.summary: The column of `e` vanishes at every vertex other than `end₁ e` and `end₂ e`.
nodes.title: Entries away from the endpoints

nodes.summary: Entry `(v, e)` is `[end₁ e = v] - [end₂ e = v]`.
nodes.title: Entries of the oriented incidence matrix

nodes.summary: The real `V × E` matrix of the multigraph with endpoint maps `end₁ end₂`: column `e` is `+1` at `end₁ e` and `-1` at `end₂ e`. Distinct edges, including parallel ones, give distinct columns.
nodes.title: Oriented incidence matrix of a multigraph

nodes.summary: For a loopless finite multigraph, the rank of its real oriented incidence matrix plus the number of connected components of `underlyingGraph end₁ end₂` equals the number of vertices.
nodes.title: Incidence rank plus number of components

nodes.summary: For a loopless finite multigraph, the rank of its real oriented incidence matrix is the number of vertices minus the number of connected components of `underlyingGraph end₁ end₂`.
nodes.title: Rank of the oriented incidence matrix

nodes.summary: For a loopless finite multigraph and finitely many boundary columns `σ j • e_{b j}` with every `σ j = ±1`, the real matrix obtained by adjoining them to the oriented incidence matrix is surjective if and only if every connected component of `underlyingGraph end₁ end₂` contains the anchor `b j` of some boundary column. The components are those of the interior edges alone.
nodes.title: Surjectivity with free boundary columns

nodes.summary: An edge whose endpoints are distinct makes them adjacent in `underlyingGraph end₁ end₂`.
nodes.title: An edge joins its endpoints in the underlying graph

nodes.summary: Vertices `u` and `v` are adjacent in `underlyingGraph end₁ end₂` if and only if they are distinct and some edge joins them, in either orientation.
nodes.title: Adjacency in the underlying graph

nodes.summary: Reachability in `underlyingGraph end₁ end₂` is reachability through edges of the multigraph, `Relation.ReflTransGen` of `AdjacentUsing` on all edges.
nodes.title: Reachability in the underlying graph

nodes.summary: For endpoint maps `end₁ end₂ : E → V`, the simple graph on `V` in which distinct vertices are adjacent when some edge joins them. It forgets multiplicities and loops and is used only for connectivity.
nodes.title: Underlying simple graph of a multigraph

nodes.summary: Entry `j` of `x ᵥ* boundaryColumns b σ` is `x (b j) * σ j`.
nodes.title: Row vector times the boundary columns

nodes.summary: Entry `e` of `x ᵥ* orientedIncidence end₁ end₂` is the difference `x (end₁ e) - x (end₂ e)` across `e`.
nodes.title: Row vector times the oriented incidence matrix

nodes.summary: For a loopless multigraph with finitely many vertices, a real vector `x` satisfies `x ᵥ* orientedIncidence end₁ end₂ = 0` if and only if `x` is constant on each connected component of `underlyingGraph end₁ end₂`.
nodes.title: Left kernel of the oriented incidence matrix

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
